To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

meaningfulness, safety and availability, which are the psychological conditions of personal engagement at work, are influenced by the individual’s personal needs, the work context and the interaction of the two.
meaningful work, a safe work environment, and the availability of the self are the psychological conditions that promote personal engagement at work.
the psychological conditions of personal engagement and disengagement are meaning, safety, and self.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the conditions under which people engage and disengage their personal selves in work.
the conditions under which individuals are likely to engage or disengage in their work roles, which has implications both for work and experiences.
the conditions at work that influence people to express and employ their whole selves or to withdraw and defend their whole selves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the psychological conditions meaningfulness (i.e., the extent to which people find their work personally meaningful), safety (i.e., how people perceive their physical, psychological, and social safety at work), and availability (i.e., whether and how people feel able to use their selves in work role performances) are important to people's personal engagement at work.
personal engagement at work is a function of the meaningfulness, safety and availability of the work context.
the psychological conditions of meaningfulness, safety and availability, and their individual and organizational sources, are important to understanding personal engagement at work.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conditions of meaningfulness, safety and availability, and the processes that create and support them, are important to the personal engagement and disengagement of employees at work.
people can be engaged or disengaged at work, and that these states of being are psychologically conditioned by meaningfulness, safety and availability.
the personal engagement of workers is a dynamic process in which the individual and the work environment mutually influence each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
people are not always fully engaged at work, and that this can have important implications for the quality of their work, their experiences, and their organizations.
personal engagement and disengagement at work are not simply the result of individual psychological processes.
people are not just workers; they are people who bring their personal selves to work.
